entries.title: Man charged with murder in fatal shooting of 2 in Austin
entries.summary:
A 36-year-old man was charged with first-degree murder in the fatal shooting of two people he knew in the Austin neighborhood, Chicago police said.

Wendy Baptisme was arrested Thursday at 10:48 p.m. in the 800 block of North Parkside Avenue after he was identified as the person who shot a 47-year-old woman and a 27-year-old man inside a home on the same block, police said.

Officers said two guns were found at the scene.

Both victims, who have yet to be identified, were taken to Mount Sinai Hospital, where they were pronounced dead.

Baptisme is scheduled to appear Sunday for a detention hearing at the Leighton Criminal Courthouse. He was charged with two counts of first-degree murder, police said.

entries.title: White Sox lose to Rockies, as Guardians top Royals to clinch AL Central title
entries.summary: <p>As promised, White Sox manager Will Venable handled Saturday night at Rate Field like a playoff game, even though his club clinched a playoff two days prior.</p><p>When starting pitcher Davis Martin’s outing went off the rails early, with three first-inning runs kickstarted by his own fielding error, he pulled the longest-tenured player on the team after just two outs recorded. Despite spending his pregame session lamenting the risk that lay in playing team sparkplug Chase Meidroth through his sore left hamstring strain, Venable brought him out for a pinch-hit double to open a would-be rally in the eighth.</p><p>Nevertheless, it all fell well short.</p><p>The Sox dropped a must-win game at home against the worst-in-MLB Rockies, 9-6. And over in Kansas City, Royals ace Michael Wacha was shelled by a Guardians team that clinched the American League Central title with a decisive 11-5 victory.</p><p>On balance, a battle-tested Guardians club that has won the division now in three consecutive seasons, showed their experience with yet another September surge. Cleveland went 16-8 in September, while the Sox dropped to 11-13 to ensure their first losing month since a 1-4 showing in March.</p><p>And at first glance, the finish to the American League Central race resembles a young White Sox team getting tight late in the season as the pressure mounts. They went 2-for-9 with runners in scoring position on Saturday, with Colson Montgomery–dogged by his unwelcome place in strikeout history–punching out with the tying runs aboard in the sixth, before extinguishing an eighth-inning rally by grounding into a double play.</p><p>Still, a team that should feel tremendously proud of their year, would argue that part of the season dominated by their inexperience has already taken place.</p><p>“We had a stretch there where I think we were really pressing too much, before falling into second place and trying to hang on,” hitting coach Derek Shomon told the Sun-Times. “We were at our best when we were chasing, and we had a ‘[bleep] it’ mentality, and that's the direct message that we shared with the group in our meeting: we’ve got to get back to ‘[bleep] it.’”</p><p>In the final stretch, that mentality has stretched over to a pitching staff that is only leaning further into the patchwork manner the White Sox have pieced together all year and will carry into the playoffs.</p><p>Anthony Kay, second on the team in innings, has been available out of the bullpen on his throw days between starts. Noah Schultz, not even five months removed from being the top starter prospect in the organization, rushed in for 3 ⅓ innings of relief work on Saturday night after Martin’s outing immediately went off the rails, though he allowed a crucial pair of solo shots himself.</p><p>“The end result is really all that matters, winning games, at this point,” Schultz said. “If I need to go a couple days in a row, I’m being available for it and open to whatever.”</p><p>A four-run Rockies ninth, highlighted by Hunter Goodman’s three-run blast–his second homer of the game–off Tyler Davis turned a spirited battle into a score too lopsided to make Andrew Benintendi’s own three-run shot in the ninth relevant. And the Guardians’ dominant finish will make a division race that was controlled by the Sox from July 4 until Sept. 16 look like it always belonged to the traditional divisional power.</p><p>“We felt like we've been playing with house money,” said general manager Chris Getz, in the middle of a series loss in Cleveland that put the Guardians up in the standings for good. “What a credit to this group that they didn't really care what anyone thought. The biggest lesson is they love to play with each other. They love to compete. They've got a high level of fearlessness that has carried us to where we are.”</p><p>Where the Sox are is still the postseason, with a chance to write a whole new finish to their 2026 campaign. But when it comes to the division, a team that’s been ahead of schedule all year, still hasn’t fully arrived.</p>

entries.title: 2 wounded in Roseland shooting
entries.summary: <p>Two people were shot while inside a vehicle in the Roseland neighborhood Saturday, Chicago police said.</p><p>Police said multiple unknown men approached the car along the 500 block of East 104th Street and fired shots inside at about 5 p.m.</p><p>A 38-year-old woman suffered a gunshot wound to the leg, and a 35-year-old man was shot in the arm, according to police.</p><p>Both victims were taken to Advocate Christ Medical Center in good condition, police said.</p><p>Detectives are investigating the shooting, police said.</p>

entries.title: Man shot while inside Englewood home
entries.summary: <p>A 26-year-old man was injured after being shot Saturday afternoon in the basement of an Englewood home, Chicago police said.</p><p>An unidentified person shot the man in his left shoulder at a residence along the 7000 block of South Laflin Street at about 3:28 p.m., police said.</p><p>The wounded man was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center in fair condition, according to police.</p><p>Area 1 detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: What do I need to know about the Chicago Cubs and White Sox both being in the MLB playoffs?
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/24/cubs-clinch-postseason-marlins-wild-card-seeding-still-a-mystery" target="_blank" ><u>Cubs</u></a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/24/white-sox-clinch-first-playoff-berth-since-2021-with-9-1-blowout-win-over-royals" target="_blank" ><u>Sox</u></a> both are in the Major League Baseball playoffs, thanks to their victories Thursday afternoon. While it’s rare for both Chicago teams to play in the postseason in the same year, it has happened before.</p><p>But it's the first time they've clinched playoff berths on the same day.</p><p>Here’s what you need to know about both teams being in the playoffs.</p><h3>In what other years have the Cubs and Sox made the postseason in the same year? What happened?</h3><p>The Cubs and Sox made the postseason together in the 2020 COVID-shortened season, and in 2008 and 1906, when they met in the World Series.</p><p>In 2020, both teams lost in the best-of-three wild-card round. The Cubs lost to the Marlins 2-0, and the Sox lost to the then-Oakland A’s 2-1.</p><p>In 2008, both teams lost in the best-of-five Division Series. The Cubs had the best record in the National League that season, but they lost to the Dodgers 3-0. The Sox lost to the Rays 3-1.</p><p>In 1906, the Sox beat the Cubs 4-2 in the World Series.</p><h3>Will either the Cubs or White Sox have any home games for the playoffs?</h3><p>Based on Saturday's games, we now know that neither team will play in Chicago in the best-of-three Wild Card Series, the first round of the postseason.</p><p>The Cubs will face the Padres in that series starting Tuesday, and all the games will be in San Diego. </p><p>The Sox also will be traveling, facing either the Houston Astros or Texas Rangers, depending on the outcome of Sunday's games.</p><p>For games to be played at Wrigley Field or at Rate Field, the Cubs or Sox would have to advance beyond the first round.</p><h3>Could there be a Red Line cross-town doubleheader during the playoffs?</h3><p>A Red Line/cross-town doubleheader is when the Cubs and Sox play on the same day at home, and it’s possible for fans to attend both games by taking the Red Line L (the subway) between Wrigley Field on Chicago’s North Side and Rate Field on the South Side.</p><p>There would not be a Red Line doubleheader in the wild-card round because the Cubs and Sox each will play all games on the road in that round. If they both advance, it becomes possible that they’d both host postseason games on the same day.</p><h3>Who’s won more World Series — Cubs or Sox?<b> </b></h3><p>They’ve each won three times. The Sox in 1906, 1917 and 2005. The Cubs in 1907, 1908 and 2016.</p><h3>What makes the Cubs team special? </h3><p>PCA is MVP: Pete Crow-Armstrong has had one of the best individual seasons in history, hitting 40+ home runs, stealing 40+ bases and playing Gold Glove defense in center field. The likely National League MVP is the most exciting reason to tune in.</p><p>Defense wins championships? The Cubs have scored the most runs in baseball this season, but their defense is what makes them stand out, with five Gold Glove winners in their daily lineup.</p><p>“Chicago tough”: Third baseman Alex Bregman’s swung a remarkably hot bat in the second half of the season and is back in action just days after taking a foul ball to the face.</p><h3>What makes the White Sox team special?</h3><p>Will’s boys don’t quit: The White Sox have 35 comeback victories, and their 11 walk-off victories are the most in the American League.</p><p>Strokin’ is more than just a song: White Sox lead the American League in runs per game, and their 204 home runs are the most a Sox team has hit since 2012.</p><p>As Colson Montgomery once put it, “We don’t know what we don’t know”: The average position player age for the Sox is 25.8, the lowest in the American League. Randal Grichuk and Andrew Benintendi are typically the only members of the Sox lineup older than 26.</p><h3>The Sox are doing well this year, but just how bad have they been in the past?</h3><p>Pretty bad. From 2023 to 2025, the Sox lost more than 100 games each season. In 2024, the Sox went 41-121, setting the modern MLB record for losses in a season. The team also lost at least 100 games in <a class="Link" href="https://southsideshowdown.com/posts/100-losses-chicago-white-sox-together-often" target="_blank" ><u>2018 and 1970</u></a>.</p><div It’s located in the middle of a lively residential neighborhood.</p><p>Meanwhile, the Sox play at <a class="Link" href="https://www.mlb.com/whitesox/ballpark/information/history-and-dimensions" target="_blank" ><u>Rate Field</u></a>, a modern stadium that opened in 1991 after Comiskey Park, its former home for 80 years, was demolished. ‘Sox Park,’ as many Chicagoans still call it with disregard to its corporate name, is on the South Side in Bridgeport, a more historically industrial area.</p><p>While Wrigleyville, home to Wrigley Field, also has working-class history, it began gentrifying in the 1980s and is more upmarket now.</p><p>The Cubs have more financial resources than the Sox. <a class="Link" href="https://www.forbes.com/teams/chicago-cubs/" target="_blank" ><u>The Cubs</u></a> were valued at $5 billion by Forbes in 2026 with revenue of $599 million. entries.title: Cubs’ wild-card matchup set: It’s a best-of-three series against Padres in San Diego
entries.summary: <p>ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> finally know which team they’ll play in their National League wild-card series and where the games will be held.</p><p>The Padres defeated the Diamondbacks late Saturday to clinch the top wild-card spot (No. 4 seed) in the NL playoffs. Coupled with the Phillies’ loss to the Rays, that locked the Cubs into the second wild-card spot (No. 5 seed), sending them to San Diego for a best-of-three series starting Tuesday.</p><p>The Cubs held the head-to-head tiebreaker against the Padres but won’t be able to catch them now. They are two games behind them in the standings with one game left in the regular season: a weather-shifted matchup against the Red Sox on Sunday in St. Petersburg.</p><p>The Cubs hold the tiebreaker with the Phillies, so even though the teams could finish with the same record, the Cubs have clinched the No. 5 seed. The Phillies still aren’t assured of a playoff spot. The Diamondbacks could catch them with a victory Sunday against the Padres should the Phillies lose again and would get in as the No. 6 seed, courtesy of a tiebreaker.</p><p>The Cubs will have no seeding or potential home-field advantage to play for Sunday and can start drawing up plans for their series against the Padres, the same team they faced — and defeated — in the wild-card round a season ago. That series, however, was played at Wrigley Field.</p><p>The Cubs won five of the six games they played against the Padres during the regular season, including a 23-3 blowout victory in the most recent meeting that saw them <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/01/cubs-dansby-swanson-home-runs-rbis-padres-offense-lineup-craig-counsell-nico-hoerner-pete-crow-armstrong-michael-conforto" target="_blank" >hit a record-setting eight home runs</a>, including three by Dansby Swanson, who drove in eight runs by himself.</p>

entries.title: Johan Gomez scores the lone goal in Fire's win at Charlotte
entries.summary: <p>CHARLOTTE, N.C. — Johan Gómez scored his first career goal in the second half to back a clean sheet from Josh Cohen in his first start for Chicago, and the Fire finished a season sweep of Charlotte FC with a 1-0 victory on Saturday night.</p><p>Chicago (12-8-6) pulled within a point of fourth-place Charlotte (12-8-7) in the Eastern Conference. The top four earn homefield advantage in the best-of-3 first round of the playoffs.</p><p>Charlotte had gone 5-0-3 since losing 2-1 to the Fire at Soldier Field to start August.</p><p>Gómez used an assist from defender Jack Elliott off a corner kick from Philip Zinckernagel in the 58th minute to give Chicago a 1-0 lead in his fourth MLS match.</p><p>Djibril Diani missed a chance to tie it when his shot hit the left post in the 59th.</p><p>The 34-year-old Cohen needed to make just one save for the shutout in his third career start. He made two starts and three appearances for Atlanta United in 2024.</p><p>Kristijan Kahlina finished with eight saves for Charlotte. Kahlina had six saves in a scoreless first half — three of them in a 5-minute span — and Cohen wasn’t tested.</p><p>Chicago had lost two straight entering play following a seven-match unbeaten run. The Fire improve to 5-4-5 on the road.</p><p>Defender Tim Ream was tagged with a red card in second-half stoppage time and will miss the next match for Charlotte, which falls to 7-3-4 at home.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Chicago: Hosts Vancouver Whitecaps on Oct. 6.</p><p>Charlotte: Hosts FC Dallas on Oct. 10.</p>

entries.title: Man hospitalized after being shot while inside car in Roseland
entries.summary: <p>A 26-year-old man was wounded in a shooting in Roseland on Saturday, Chicago police said. </p><p>The victim was inside a vehicle along the 100 block of East 114th Place at about 4:55 p.m. when he was shot by an unidentified man, police said.</p><p>The victim, who sustained a gunshot wound to the thigh, was taken to Advocate Christ Medical Center, according to police.</p><p>He was initially reported in fair condition.</p>

entries.title: Blackhawks' Anton Frondell progresses toward A-game in victorious preseason finale
entries.summary: <p>Blackhawks rookie Anton Frondell didn't enter training camp riding the same high as when he joined the team for the last month of last season.</p><p>But during two weeks of camp, he has inched toward to that level again. He scored the opening goal and was noticeably better in the Hawks' 3-2 win over the Blues in their preseason finale Saturday.</p><p>Coach Jeff Blashill, who admitted Friday that Frondell hadn't gotten to his "A-game" yet, saw what he wanted to see from the Swedish power forward.</p><p>"He’s a young guy that wants to be great," Blashill said. "That’s a great thing. That means he’s ultimately going to reach his ceiling... [But] he just wants to be perfect. Sometimes you just got to free yourself up a little bit. I thought he did a better job of that tonight. </p><p>"I [had] tons of belief in him even through the first couple [preseason] games, when he probably wasn’t playing his best. I knew there was way better, and it showed tonight. He’s a horse who can make a play. That’s a pretty good combo."</p><p>Frondell also liked his performance in his 22-plus minutes of ice time, which led team forwards.</p><p>He stuffed the box score by attempting eight shots (getting four on goal) and taking 22 faceoffs (although he won only seven). He scored in the first period after actually losing a faceoff; Tyler Bertuzzi got to the puck first and created a juicy rebound that Frondell buried.</p><p>"I would say this was my best game during those three [preseason games]," Frondell said. "I felt like I had more speed today, had some good chances and also ended up with a goal. Power play worked out better.</p><p>"[When] we end up playing five-on-five back to the smaller ice here in North America, [I] have to switch a little bit my game style. I'm getting used to it, and today felt like I was more back."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">GOAL: Anton Frondell slaps in a shot from the slot to open the scoring. <a href="https://t.co/02UWa5Uc2J">pic.twitter.com/02UWa5Uc2J</a></p>— BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) <a href="https://x.com/BlackhawksFocus/status/2103988460084195576?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">September 26, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Teuvo Teravainen and Ethan Del Mastro, two Hawks fighting desperately for opening-night jobs, also stood out in positive ways. Ryan Donato and Oliver Moore, two Hawks with seemingly more secure jobs, both struggled with defensive-zone turnovers. </p><p>That's sometimes the way it goes in the preseason, which the Hawks finished 2-1-1. The team now has a couple days to finalize their roster before flying to Las Vegas ahead of their regular-season opener Tuesday.</p><h3><b>Boisvert’s identity</b></h3><p>Hawks forward prospect Sacha Boisvert is already an NHL-caliber fighter — there's no doubt about that. He might even be a professional boxing-level fighter. Blues veteran Nathan Walker found that out the hard way Thursday.</p><p>Boisvert didn't appear NHL-ready in other aspects of the game during camp, however, despite holding his own in his first seven NHL appearances last spring. He will start the season in Rockford with quite a bit to prove.</p><p>"I don’t know if he’s a better center or wing," Blashill said. "We’re still trying to figure that piece of it out. I think he’s also got to then figure out, 'How am I going to make myself a difference-maker at this level?'</p><p>Blashill lauded Boisvert's fighting skills but said he wasn't physical enough or effective enough in puck battles, especially earlier on in camp.</p><p>"He has to go to Rockford and keep finding that identity of what’s going to make him special as a pro," Blashill added.</p>

entries.title: 2026-27 NHL bold predictions: Youth revolution overtakes league, but Blackhawks fall short of playoffs
entries.summary: <p>Critics of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a>’ rebuild as a fundamental concept were quieted last season.</p><p>Although the Hawks’ rebuild took only a modest step forward — and it remains unclear whether it ultimately will succeed — it was a good year for their youthful peers around the NHL. The recently rebuilt Canadiens and Ducks made playoff runs, and the almost-done-rebuilding Sharks made a huge leap.</p><p>Those three teams became a few of the most exciting in the league, and they should remain compelling this season. Can the Canadiens, for example, establish themselves in the top tier of the Eastern Conference?</p><p>Can Leo Carlsson and his crew of suddenly rich young forwards keep the Ducks’ magic going? Can Macklin Celebrini live up to the Connor McDavid-level hype and lift the Sharks into the playoffs?</p><p>And can the Hawks join that wave? Internally, they think they’re about to do so. Proofs of concept, showing it can happen in this era, now exist. But analytics models, betting lines and talking heads are skeptical.</p><p>On the other end of the age spectrum, a handful of teams — including the Panthers, Rangers, Penguins, Predators, Jets and Kings — enter this season relying on over-the-hump cores to keep them competitive.</p><p>For the Hawks, Ducks, Sharks and Canadiens to make further inroads into the hierarchy, they’ll need those aging teams to crash out. And it feels as though they might.</p><p>Here are my bold predictions for the 2026-27 NHL standings:</p><h3><b>Central Division</b></h3><p><b>1. Wild (114 points):</b> Quinn Hughes will sign a lengthy contract, win the Norris Trophy and not only help the Wild surge to the top of the Central’s three-headed monster but also win the Presidents’ Trophy.</p><p><b>2. Stars (110):</b> Jason Robertson’s looming free agency is concerning, but the balanced Stars will remain contenders for at least one more season.</p><p><b>3. Avalanche (105): </b>The Avalanche learned they need to expend less energy during the regular season. After coasting until April, they’ll turn it on and bowl through the league in the playoffs.</p><p><b>4. Mammoth (94):</b> The up-and-coming Mammoth seem more likely to finish fourth in the Central than any other team is to finish in any given spot in its division. That’s exactly what will happen.</p><p><b>5. Blues (91): </b>The Blues will turn out better than last season but worse than in 2024-25, leading to a narrow playoff miss.</p><p><b>6. Blackhawks (85):</b> The Hawks’ internal playoff ambitions feel unlikely to be fulfilled, but their youth (and close-game luck) will improve enough to get them out of the league basement and maintain the fan base’s tentative long-term optimism.</p><p><b>7. Jets (81):</b> Goalie Connor Hellebuyck’s departure will be felt dramatically, on and off the ice. He has covered up flaws in Winnipeg for a while.</p><p><b>8. Predators (74):</b> It will become clear the Predators’ second-half push last season was a mirage once they careen off the age cliff this season.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div entries.title: Dear Abby: Father and son chefs torn apart by alcohol addiction
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I am a retired executive chef, divorced for many years with three adult children. My son was also an executive chef but no longer. He is a mean alcoholic. He stays drunk when not at his job, and he says cruel and nasty things to all family members. His older sister has written him off because of all the hurtful things he has said about her and her family. He calls me when he is drunk and wants to talk about cooking, though he hates it. He doesn't listen to me at all and just goes on and on. His mother passed three years ago, and he has never gotten over it. He was her favorite.</p><p>I love my son very much but can't talk with him anymore as it upsets me for days after. How can I get him to seek counseling? He won't listen to anyone. He admits that he has an alcohol problem but chooses to do nothing about it. The only other family member who still talks to him is his younger sister, and he is mean to her as well. What can we do to help him? — <i>ANGUISHED DAD IN TEXAS</i></p><p><b>DEAR DAD:</b> I am sorry for your pain, but you cannot force your son to deal with his alcohol addiction. Until he faces the full consequences of what it is costing him — in other words, hits rock bottom — he will do nothing about it. I hope you will consider visiting some Al-Anon meetings, which you can find by going to al-anon.org/info. These meetings are everywhere, and you should have little difficulty finding one. If you do, you will find other parents, spouses, siblings and friends of alcoholics who are trying to deal with the same issues as you.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My husband and I have been married for 26 years. I have often felt as if we were growing apart, finding interests in different things. We seem unable to discuss our emotions without one of us getting hurt feelings and the talk devolving into awful arguments. There has never been any real question of extramarital affairs.</p><p>One night, I playfully asked if I could go through his computer. He immediately became defensive, saying he just doesn't like people getting into his computer, messing with his stuff. I get that. I wouldn't want just anybody getting into my computer, either. However, I am not just anybody; I'm his wife. He has full access to all of my computers, phones and digital accessories. Why do I feel like he's got something to hide? I don't know what to do. — <i>PRESUMPTION OF GUILT</i></p><p><b>DEAR PRESUMPTION:</b> Pressing your husband on this issue right now will only lead to more arguments. If you want to repair the marriage, you both need to learn to communicate more effectively. Without mentioning his computer, invite your husband to see a licensed family therapist with you. If he refuses, go without him. If he agrees, work on the basics now and save the privacy issues and your suspicions for future sessions.</p><p><i>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.</i></p>

entries.title: Eagles' Jalen Hurts unlike any QB Bears have seen this year
entries.summary: <p>The first quarterback the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> faced this season was the rarest of quarterbacks — a No. 1 overall pick so unimpressive his team didn’t extend his contract before the final year of his rookie deal.</p><p></p><p>The second had started just 14 games in the previous five seasons.</p><p></p><p>The third, former Super Bowl MVP Jalen Hurts, will be a significant step up in class <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/26/bears-need-rushing-attack-to-lead-way-against-eagles-just-like-last-season" target="_blank" >Monday night</a>. It will be a telling test drive for a defense that’s already shown signs of leaking oil.</p><p></p><p>One week after a rainstorm served as a 12<sup>th</sup> man for both defenses, a Bears unit that gave up 37 points in the opener will face their best quarterback to date — and maybe until they see Drake Maye a month from now.</p><p></p><p>"It's his ability to run of out the pocket, and just keep the play alive — and his deep ball," safety Dillon Thieneman said.</p><p></p><p>The Eagles offense has underwhelmed in two wins this season under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, but Hurts has a 100.7 passer rating and ranks 11<sup>th</sup> in passing yards. His ability to run, though, is what most concerns defensive coordinator Dennis Allen.</p><p></p><p>“When everything goes according to plan and he's in a quick rhythm, he gets the ball out, throws the ball well, does all those things that you have to do at the quarterback position,” Allen said. “It's really when things break down, and it doesn't go as planned, that's where he can really hurt you with his feet. That will definitely be a big part of what we have to contend with.”</p><p></p><p>His rushing skills go far beyond the “Tush Push,” too. He ran for 421 yards last year — more than Caleb Williams — and for eight touchdowns.</p><p></p><p>That running ability opens up opportunities for Hurts to throw deep — and wide.</p><p></p><p>Last year, his nine intended air yards per pass was the second-highest in the NFL. He has 279 yards when throwing outside the numbers this season and a 72% completion percentage that ranks fourth-highest in the league, per NFL Next Gen Stats.</p><p></p><p>The Bears’ outside cornerbacks need to answer this week’s test better than they did in Week 1. Against the Panthers, the Bears gave up three touchdowns and 196 yards on throws outside the numbers. Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson allowed a 113.7 and perfect 158.3 passer rating, respectively.</p><p></p><p>“For us, it’s just, 'Continue to get better,'” Johnson said.</p><p></p><p>On “Black Friday” last year, Hurts went 19-for-34 passing for 230 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in a loss to the Bears. A.J. Brown, who was responsible for all but 98 of the Eagles’ receiving yards, now plays for the Patriots. Tight end Dallas Goedert, their third-leading receiver last year, won’t play Monday because of a knee injury.</p><p></p><p>Saquon Barkley, of course, remains. Two years removed from a 2,005-yard rushing season, he’s been underwhelming over two games, rushing just 19 times for 92 yards.</p><p></p><p>“If you go low, he’ll jump,” Allen said. “If you stop your feet, he can go around you. He’s still fast and explosive and he can juke. There’s not really anything that he can’t do.”</p><p></p><p>Like Barkley, Hurts’ reputation precedes him.</p><p></p><p>“We know who he is — we know the success that he’s had,” Johnson said. “Just trying to get him rattled, trying to get him a little antsy in the pocket and things like that. Ultimately, like any other quarterback, you gotta hit him, gotta make him uncomfortable.”<br></p>

entries.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams' has a Grade 2 hamstring strain: report
entries.summary: <p>Quarterback Caleb Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring strain, ESPN reported Sunday, which lines up with the what the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> have have laid out since he was injured one week ago.</p><p>There’s no one-size-fits-all timeline for recovery, but Grade 2 strains typically require an absence of three or four weeks. Had Williams’ timeline been longer, the Bears would have put him on injured reserve, which requires players to miss four games. They did not.</p><p>After he was hurt, Bears coach Ben Johnson called Williams “week-to-week” and said he’d be out for “some time,” which eliminated him as an option for Monday’s game against the Eagles. The Bears host the Jets on Sunday but an obvious target for Williams’ return would be the following week against the rival Packers in Green Bay.</p><p>Williams didn't practice all last week and was officially ruled out on Saturday's injury report. The Bears will start either <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/26/bears-qb-tyson-bagent-clears-concussion-protocol-start-eagles-case-keenum-ben-johnson" target="_blank" >Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum against the Eagles.</a></p><p>On Monday, Johnson pointed to Williams’ ability to heal quickly as a reason to be optimistic he wouldn’t be out for long.</p><p>“He gets back -- he has in the past -- a lot faster than what people can anticipate,” he said.</p>

entries.summary: <p>Two people were hospitalized for smoke inhalation after an apartment fire in North Lawndale early Sunday, Chicago Fire Department officials said.</p><p>Firefighters responded to a fire at a residential building in the 2200 block of South Keeler Avenue at about 5:30 a.m., according to fire officials.</p><p>T</p><p>A 71-year-old woman and a 48-year-old man were taken to Stroger Hospital and Mount Sinai Hospital, respectively, for smoke inhalation, according to Chicago Police.</p><p>The woman was listed in critical condition, and the man was in good condition, police said.</p><p>The fire was extinguished by about 6:13 a.m., fire officials said.</p><p>No other injuries were reported. entries.title: Trump appears Sunday at the Presidents Cup golf tournament in suburban Medinah
entries.summary: <p>President Donald Trump addressed the crowd at Sunday’s Presidents Cup golf tournament in suburban Medinah, saying “Our country is doing great, better than ever before.”</p><p>Hundreds gathered at the first hole of the tournament, where Trump lauded the country’s position under his leadership and said he was looking forward to watching golf pros.</p><p>The crowd chanted “USA, USA, USA” before he took the stage, and spectators shook red, white and blue pom poms and American flags.</p><p>Trump greeted and shook hands with each pair of U.S. and international team members before they started the fifth and final round of the tournament, which started Thursday at the Medinah Country Club.</p><p>Trump was serving as the tournament’s honorary chairman, which he also did in 2017 at Liberty National Golf Club in New Jersey during his first presidency.</p><p>It’s the first time Trump has visited Illinois in his second presidency. Last time he was in the state was his inflammatory visit to the National Association of Black Journalists conference in Chicago in 2024, where he responded combatively to the moderator’s questions and ridiculed his opponent, then-Vice President Kamala Harris, for being biracial.</p><p>“I didn’t know she was Black until a number of years ago when she happened to turn Black, and now she wants to be known as Black. So I don’t know, is she Indian or is she Black?” Trump said at the time.</p><p>Harris is Black and Indian, born in Oakland, California to an Indian mother and Jamaican father.</p><p>A handful of demonstrators, both pro- and anti-Trump, gathered around 9:30 a.m. Sunday outside the tournament before Trump arrived.</p>

entries.title: Hard to find a good kosher candy to throw at your kids
entries.summary: <p>To be a Chicagoan — yes, I know I'm not — is to have a certain nostalgia about candy.</p><p>Growing up here — OK, I grew up near Cleveland, thank you for noticing — meant to be aware of the enormous Brach's factory on the West Side and the Spanish Revival Mars confectionery on Oak Park Avenue. Visits downtown were liable to give you a contact high from the cocoa aroma rolling off the Blommer's chocolate factory.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-7e0000" name="module-7e0000"></a> <div class="RichTextSidebarModule-title">Opinion bug</div> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h2>Opinion</h2></div> </div><p>Being a fat kid — try snatching <i>that</i>away from me, you touchy chauvinists — I had a visceral understanding of the entire Brach's line. The gorgeous slightly soft, matte milk chocolate stars. The shiny dark blobs of bridge mix, with its scorned peanuts and ultra vanilla creams.</p><p>My mother played bridge — yes, in Berea, immediately west of Cleveland, geez, give it a rest, will ya? — and I would belly crawl, like soldiers on the "Combat!" TV show, into the living room, to snake my hand into a bowl and retrieve a fistful of mix, then scuttle back to my room to enjoy my prize. What a sight that must have been.</p><p>And we — meaning Chicagoans and whatever unwanted interlopers manage to jam themselves among them — shouldn't complain. Despite the insane sugar tariffs sending Chicago candy companies fleeing to Mexico, we still have a bounty: Ferrara Pan, churning out their vastly cool Nerds Gummy Clusters. Butterfingers and Baby Ruths are made in Franklin Park, which is not Chicago either, last time I checked.</p><p>Some folks insist Tootsie Rolls are made in Chicago, though after a lifetime of being denied access to the factory, I hope you will forgive me for insisting Tootsie Rolls are actually made in the military dictatorship of Myanmar, excreted by emotionally-damaged French poodles trapped in inhumanely small crates and force fed a combination of high fructose corn system, industrial waste and the offal of rabbits who died testing cosmetics.</p><p>Is the above an unfair fiction? It's not like Tootsie Roll is going to complain.</p><p>But I haven't gotten to the point yet. The point is Sunkist Fruit Gems have been discontinued. The news has been pinballing across the internet all last week.</p><p>That stings. If you aren't Jewish —- well, I should play the overwhelming odds here — <i>since</i> you aren't Jewish, you might not know the deep cultural significance of Sunkist Fruit Gems. They're kosher, brightly colored and individually wrapped, with a pivotal role in certain obscure Jewish rituals.</p><p>Such as the <i>Aufruf.</i> No idea, right? I've participated in one. Before a couple is married, the groom-to-be is called up at a Saturday service to read the blessing of the Torah. Then afterward, the groom — or in these more equitable times, the bride and groom — is pelted with candy. I have a vague memory of shielding myself with my tallis. My wife and I also pelted our kids with Sunkist Fruit Gems at their bar mitzvahs — I remember being tempted to put a little pepper, a certain sidearm snap, into my throw. And also, before my speech, I popped a Gem in my mouth, for the sugar boost.</p><p>There's no sense to what survives and what doesn't. History teaches us the good vanish while the subpar persist. Remember Drostes chocolate? You could buy a foil covered Drostes chocolate orange —delicious orange-flavored chocolate spheres that fall into segments when tapped briskly on a table. Try to find one now. Meanwhile, Milk Way bars — overly sweet lozenges of meh hardly worth the effort required to chew them — are everywhere.</p><p>Not the end of the world, I know. With Gaza the new Killing Christ (the pretext by which you can do whatever you want to whatever Jews you find and still feel you enjoy the moral high ground), the elimination of Sunkist Fruit Gems might seem trivial. But at least there is consolation. CandyFavorites.com sells Fruit Gems knock-offs, such as Pizazz Fruit Slices.</p><p>I don't want to make too much of this. There's good news, too: This is the part of the column where I planned to deliver the bad news about Jewish population decline due to assimilation. The hedge fund that bought Sunkist Fruit Gems can't bother to market the confections because there aren't enough Jews to buy them.</p><p>But the surprising good news, according to the Pew Research Foundation, is the religion is "keeping pace" with the general population. Plus, on Saturday, Sunkist announced on their Instagram feed that "Sunkist Fruit Gems are not going anywhere" and will be back on shelves "very soon."</p><p>Interesting if true, as my people — that would be journalists — say. At least cause for hope. And really, with a little hope, and something sweet to look forward to, Jews can soldier through almost any crisis.</p>

entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> will begin Chicago's postseason doubleheader Tuesday with Game 1 of their wild-card series at 4 p.m., and the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> will open their series at 9 p.m., MLB announced Sunday.</p><p>Whether the Sox play in Houston or Arlington, Texas, the first two games of their series are scheduled for 4 p.m. Likewise, Games 1 and 2 of the Cubs' series in San Diego are scheduled for 9 p.m.</p><p>Peacock, NBC's streaming service, and NBC Sports Network will carry both series. entries.title: Man charged with attempted murder in Saturday stabbing
entries.summary: <p>A 43-year-old man has been charged with first-degree attempted murder and two felony charges of aggravated battery after he was identified as the person who stabbed a man on the Near South Side early Saturday, Chicago police said.</p><p>Police said Hector Uriostegui was arrested at about 12:04 a.m. Satruday in the 3600 block of North Newland Avenue.</p><p>He had been identified as the person who stabbed and seriously wounded a 32-year-old man 15 minutes earlier in the 2200 block of South Michigan Avenue, police said.</p><p>Uriostegui has a detention hearing set for Sunday at the Leighton Criminal Courthouse, police said.</p>

entries.title: Sky’s Sydney Taylor named to AP All-Rookie team
entries.summary: <p>Sydney Taylor has her first major award under her belt. The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> guard was named to the AP All-Rookie Team on Sunday, joining AP Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles, the Wings’ Azzi Fudd, the Storm’s Flau’jae Johnson, the Liberty’s Pauline Astier, and the Tempo’s Kiki Rice.</p><p>Taylor averaged 13.6 points and 2 assists in 37 games this season. Once she moved into the starting rotation, her scoring jumped to 15.4 points.</p><p>Taylor was one of the big break-out stories of the year as she went undrafted out of college and had played the previous two years overseas. Now a much bigger profile and payday are coming.</p><p>Taylor will be a reserved free agent this offseason, meaning she can only negotiate with the Sky. She told the Sun-Times that she’s interested in signing a multi-year deal with the team.</p>

entries.title: Man, 23, wounded in Ashburn shooting
entries.summary: <p>A 23-year-old man was wounded in a shooting in the Ashburn neighborhood late Saturday, Chicago police said.</p><p>Police said the man was walking in the 8200 block of South Whipple Street at about 10:14 p.m. Saturday when he was shot.</p><p>A black sedan had pulled alongside him and an unknown assailant fired shots from inside the car before fleeing in an unknown direction, police said.</p><p>The man suffered a gunshot wound to his left leg and was taken to Advocate Christ Medical Center in fair condition, according to police.</p><p>Area One Detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Bears' next opponent: Jets fall 31-24 as Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs scores 3 touchdowns
entries.summary: <p>DETROIT — Jahmyr Gibbs had a go-ahead 11-yard reception with 2:25 left for his third touchdown of the game and the Detroit Lions held on to beat the New York Jets 31-24 on Sunday.</p><p>The Lions (2-1) leaned on Gibbs a lot — on the ground and through the year — and he delivered another fantastic performance. The dynamic running back had 20 carries for 99 yards with 17- and 1-yard touchdown runs in the second half, along with seven receptions for 65 yards and score.</p><p>The Jets (1-2) overcame a 14-point deficit in the fourth quarter with Geno Smith's 4-yard touchdown pass to Jeremy Ruckert, a 23-yard throw to Garrett Wilson and a 2-point conversion pass to Sterling Shepard to make it 24-all.</p><p>New York's defense — led by head coach Aaron Glenn, Detroit's former defensive coordinator — then had two blown coverages as Goff and Gibbs marched the Lions down the field to quickly regain the lead.</p><p>With a chance to tie or perhaps go for the win, the Jets were on the Detroit 28 when Smith lost a fumble after blitzing safety Chuck Clark sacked him. That sealed it for the Lions.</p><p>Smith finished 31 of 37 for 321 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Wilson had 10 catches for 107 yards and a TD, but was on the sideline on the final offensive play after getting banged up.</p><p>Goff was 25 of 32 for 269 yards with two touchdowns and no turnovers.</p><p>The Lions got off to a slow start against Glenn, who was Dan Campbell's defensive coordinator from 2021 through 2024. Detroit put the ball in Gibbs' hands to set up Jake Bates' 30-yard field goal early in the second quarter.</p><p>New York's offense suddenly started moving the ball on the ensuing possession as Smith completed passes on four straight snaps for 72 yards. Rookie Kenyon Sadiq fully extended on a 24-yard touchdown catch in tight coverage put the Jets up 7-3. Sadiq had seven receptions for 105 yards and the score.</p><p>Detroit converted a fourth-and-2 from the New York 9 with a pass to Isaac TeSlaa to set up Goff's 4-yard toss to Amon-Ra St. Brown's back shoulder for a 10-7 lead late in the first half.</p><p>It extended Goff's streak with a touchdown pass to 26 games and was St. Brown's fifth catch for a score in 10 quarters this season.</p><h3>Injuries</h3><p><b>Jets:</b> RB Breece Hall left with a thigh injury. ... LG Dylan Parham hurt a knee.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Jets:</b> Face the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" >Bears</a> at Soldier Field next Sunday.</p><p><b>Lions:</b> At Carolina next Sunday night.</p>

entries.title: Bears' QB situation gets overly convoluted as they sort out options after Caleb Williams' hamstring injury
entries.summary: <p>A complicated quarterback situation has turned into a circus for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a> as they sort out their near future with starter <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/11/as-engineer-and-artist-blend-styles-bears-ben-johnson-gets-goosebumps-about-future-with-caleb-williams" >Caleb Williams</a>, backup Tyson Bagent and third-stringer Case Keenum.</p><p>Keenum will start Monday against the Eagles, Fox reported, despite Bagent clearing concussion protocol Sunday. The Bears updated Bagent’s game status from questionable to completely available, he was in meetings late in the week and practiced in full Saturday, but will be Keenum’s backup.</p><p>Miller Moss, an undrafted rookie, is expected to be promoted Monday from the practice squad to be the emergency quarterback.</p><p>The Bears ruled out Williams on Saturday, an inevitable move that could’ve been done days earlier, but throughout the situation, the reality has been they don’t know when he’ll be back. The possibility of missing a month or so is always on the table for an injury like that.</p><p>Some of this mess was avoidable.</p><p>The first mistake was coach Ben Johnson initially casting Williams’ hamstring injury as something that might not cost him even one game even though he already knew Williams wouldn’t be able to practice all week. Johnson probably intended it as a salute to Williams’ toughness, but it fueled backlash that Williams had overreacted as he was carted to the locker room at Soldier Field.</p><p>The idea of him playing one week after suffering even a low-grade hamstring strain was implausible.</p><p>Williams actually has a Grade 2 hamstring strain, NFL Network reported Sunday, which could keep a player out 1-2 months, but the Bears are projecting 3-4 weeks and Williams hopes to beat that timeline.</p><p>Given that he’s out Monday and the team doesn’t plan to put him on injured reserve, which would require him to miss a minimum of four games, all of that is a roundabout way of saying he’s week-to-week, which is how Johnson has been describing it.</p><p>If the Bears change their minds about putting Williams on IR, they have until Monday at 3 p.m. for the Eagles game to count toward the four.</p><p>Williams missing up to four games shouldn’t be the end of the world because they’re approaching a relatively soft spot in the schedule. After hosting the Eagles, they’re home Sunday against the Jets, then visit the Packers on Oct. 11 and Falcons on Oct. 18.</p><p>That’s a navigable stretch to go at least 2-2 with a backup quarterback if necessary, especially considering how terrible the Packers have looked, and hope to be .500 or better when Williams is healthy.</p><p>That backup should be Bagent, who has decisively been the No. 2 quarterback over Keenum the last two seasons.</p><p>If Bagent is cleared to play, he should start. There shouldn’t be legitimate concern about his readiness after coaches said multiple times last week he was in the loop on game planning and he now has gotten a green light from the medical staff.</p><p>Johnson was all over the place on Bagent’s status Saturday, perhaps intentionally to maintain some mystery for the Eagles. He errantly said twice before practice that he had cleared concussion protocol, leading to the team issuing a clarification.</p><p>He dodged a question about whether he needed to see something from Bagent in practice to make a decision on a starter. He said, “There's a reason why Tyson was the backup as we ended camp,” and added that since he was in meetings and able to practice, Bagent was “right on track to be where he needs to be” and “in a good spot for what we're asking him to do.”</p><p>Then when asked if he might start Keenum against the Eagles and use Bagent as the backup, he replied, “Sure.”</p><p>Keenum, 38, was brought in last year predominantly to mentor Williams and Bagent and has been a huge asset in that regard, but has not thrown a pass in a game since playing for the Texans in 2023 and rarely, if ever, practiced against a first-team defense before stepping in last week.</p><p>The Bears have long viewed Bagent as an emerging starter and repeatedly said last offseason he was too valuable to trade away for a draft pick. He got a two-year, $10 million contract extension last year that covers this season and next, and he’s the NFL’s 13th-highest paid backup.</p><p>They believed Bagent was an ideal insurance policy for Williams and that losing their starter for any period wouldn’t automatically wreck their season.</p><p>The Bears are an underdog Monday — multiple players brought it up the last few days — but playing the better quarterback gives them a better shot. It’d be different if Bagent’s status had been uncertain all the way up to kickoff, but Johnson seemed to consider him an option no later than Saturday. He might’ve been fairly confident in that even earlier, saying Wednesday the Bears didn’t need to bring in an extra quarterback even as an emergency option.</p><p>It never needed to become this convoluted publicly. It’s doubtful the Bears actually gained any advantage over the Eagles by dancing around all of this, and the plan for Monday is, at minimum, debatable.</p>

entries.title: Battles for Blackhawks' forward jobs will continue into season, even with Landon Slaggert on waivers
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> entered training camp with 24 players in their NHL group, knowing they'd need to eventually cut one.</p><p>They made that decision Sunday, placing forward Landon Slaggert on waivers, per PuckPedia. The Hawks will hope to slip Slaggert through to Rockford along with deep-depth forward Dominic Toninato, who joined him on waivers.</p><p>That means the Hawks will presumably bring 13 forwards, eight defensemen — including both Kevin Korchinski and Ethan Del Mastro — and two goalies to Las Vegas for the season opener Tuesday.</p><p>That roster isn't necessarily a finished product, though. Coach Jeff Blashill has brought up every day recently that it was difficult for players to stand out or move themselves up or down the hierarchy during this shortened training camp and preseason.</p><p>He expects the competition for spots on the roster — as well as for specific roles within it — to continue well into the regular season.</p><p>"There will be guys that are continuing to vie for where they really sit within the team all the way through October," Blashill said.</p><p>Among the forward group, those borderline guys battling for jobs are most notably Andrew Mangiapane, Teuvo Teravainen and Jordan Greenway.</p><p>Slaggert, assuming he isn't claimed off waivers, will be first in line for a call-up, with rookie AJ Spellacy also in contention. But once Connor Bedard returns, somebody else could end up on the chopping block.</p><p>Slaggert was proud of his training this summer, during which he gained 10 pounds to get up to 198 — which he thinks will help him in puck battles — and worked on his first touches, including receiving passes and picking pucks off the walls more cleanly.</p><p>Those haven't been strong suits in the past, as he has been more of a speedy, hard-working disruptor with minimal puck-handling ability. After 102 NHL appearances, the odds of him breaking out are decreasing.</p><p>Greenway, when healthy, probably has the most secure spot of those borderline forwards as a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/09/22/blackhawks-jordan-greenway-trade-defensive-acumen-wild-sabres" >big, physical presence</a> on the fourth line.</p><p>But he struggled to stay healthy the last two seasons with the Sabres and missed the second half of this camp with a lower-body injury, although Blashill expects him to be available Tuesday.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/09/22/blackhawks-jordan-greenway-trade-defensive-acumen-wild-sabres" >Jordan Greenway’s defensive acumen makes him sneaky-smart addition for Blackhawks</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>Teravainen's descent into healthy-scratch territory, meanwhile, will probably raise some eyebrows around the league. The 32-year-old Finn is coming off the worst year of his career and entering the last year of his contract, so it wouldn't be surprising if the Hawks explored trade options.</p><p>As long as he remains in Chicago, one advantage he offers is special-teams experience on both sides. He played well in the Hawks' <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/09/26/blackhawks-anton-frondell-a-game-preseason-blues-sacha-boisvert" >preseason finale</a> Saturday, using his stick to break up plays.</p><p>"When Teuvo plays confident, he’s moving his feet. And when he’s moving his feet, he’s a really good player," Blashill said. "He’s smart defensively [and] offensively. When his confidence is down, he tends to stand still with the puck more than anything else."</p><p>Mangiapane is hoping to rebound from his own frustrating, unproductive and injury-riddled 2025-26 season. He made just 10 appearances with the Hawks after the Oilers traded him in March, and he spent the first few months of the offseason simply healing up.</p><p>But he's only 30, and he's only two years removed from a 40-point season. Repeating that production might be unlikely, but scrappy style and puck-pursuit skills could be useful. He unlocked something in Anton Frondell and Tyler Bertuzzi in the preseason finale.</p><p>"Last year, there were a lot of little things going on in my life," Mangiapane said. "I'm happy to put all that behind me and really focus on hockey and getting my game back to where it used to be.</p><p>"Me being tenacious and hard working leads to that. [It's about] getting to the front of the net, getting grade-A scoring chances and hopefully scoring a few."</p>

entries.summary: <p>Florida made a massive jump in The Associated Press Top 25 on Sunday and landed in the top 10 for the first time in five years while four new teams joined the rankings in a major shuffle.</p><p>The Gators' 24-point win over then-No. 4 Mississippi under first-year coach Jon Sumrall on Saturday earned them a 13-rung promotion to No. 8, their highest ranking since 2020 and first top-10 appearance since 2021.</p><p>Texas, Georgia and Notre Dame continued to hold the top three spots, Miami was a season-high No. 4 and Ohio State moved up two spots to No. 5. entries.title: White Sox wrap up magical season with a victory, and still hope to turn the page in postseason
entries.summary: <p>In many respects, the 162nd game of the 2026 White Sox season played out like those of recent years.</p><p>The Sox’ 4-2 victory over the Rockies had zero stakes for either side, many reserves filled out the box score, and the announced home attendance for the year clocked in under two million fans (1,986,419).</p><p>The difference is the nearly 30,000 on hand for Sunday pushed the full-season figure to the highest total the White Sox have drawn since 2022; the only year they’ve eclipsed two million fans in the last 15 seasons. Rather than stick around just in case nigh anonymous pieces of the roster might toss free t-shirts into the stands, fans remained to roar in support of a White Sox club headed to Houston for the franchise’s first postseason action in five years.</p><p>It’s easy to imagine a darker White Sox context where an injured pitcher carries one of the highest Q scores on the roster, but the cheers cresting as Mike Vasil raised his fist to the crowd, his other arm around the team’s actual best player, Miguel Vargas, connoted a warm feeling about what this team has become.</p><p>“The way the fans have come out and supported these guys and given them energy,” said manager Will Venable. “To watch that back-and-forth grow throughout the season has been amazing.”</p><p>The 2026 White Sox won just 84 games, but did so in front of fans that reasoned 75 victories was an aspirational goal, and repaid the overage in enthusiasm.</p><p>Could they have won more? They certainly thought so, and rue an early-September slide that cost them a division title. They also had 11 walk-off victories, were often stringing together pitching plans that would have made MacGyver nervous, and no team that’s tied itself spiritually to the papacy the way these Sox have can consider themselves starved of blessings.</p><p>“I don't think anyone saw the kind of success that we had, and I think it was really fun to be a part of,” said Sunday’s winning pitcher Anthony Kay.</p><p>They’re also boarding their flight to Houston hoping for a reset. They went 34-33 after the All-Star break. Allowing the Guardians to catch them after winning the season series and leading the American League Central for two and a half months dealt a sting they were still shaking off Sunday.</p><p>“We were pissed,” shortstop Colson Montgomery. “We had a lot of vocal people. Everyone was just like, ‘We’ve got important games coming up.’”</p><p>Perhaps no one better represents the quest for an October rebirth than Montgomery. He socked 31 homers and dominated during the 18-10 May that launched the Sox onto the national scene, but is craving a clean slate after a poor second half and claiming an MLB single-season strikeout record he admits “you don’t want your name to be a part of.”</p><p>The White Sox dropped five of seven to the Astros this year across two series featuring some of their lowest moments, strategic moves that Venable openly second-guessed, with the most recent four-game set in Houston coming at a point in the year where players admit the club had lost its free-wheeling verve…temporarily.</p><p>“We were scuffling as a whole,” said veteran outfielder Randal Grichuk of losing three of four against the Astros. “We match up well with them.”</p><p>Are they capable of a deep playoff run? Their rotation uncertainty suggests otherwise, but that would assume anyone not aboard their flight to Houston has a hold on how and why this Sox team has been good all year; which is surely not the case.</p><p>“Our focus is just on us,” said designated hitter Andrew Benintendi. “Everybody in here knows what we can do.”</p><p>Would knocking off an 81-81 Astros team be a monumental accomplishment? No. But it’s doable. It’d be the team’s first postseason series victory in 21 years. And it’d be fun, which is the quality that brought nearly two million fans to the park this year.</p>

entries.title: Alex Bregman homers twice in season-finale win, Cubs head to playoffs aiming to ‘make some noise in October’
entries.summary: <p>ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — A week after a fouled-off baseball did <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/23/cubs-alex-bregman-face-injury-return-matt-shaw-bunt-daniel-palencia-stats" >significant damage to Alex Bregman’s face</a>, Bregman returned the favor, doling out punishment to the baseballs.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>’ third baseman launched a pair of home runs as part of a four-hit day in a 6-2 win over the Red Sox in the regular-season finale Sunday, showing the type of impact he can make as the team eyes a deep playoff run.</p><p>“I did want to feel good before the playoffs,” Bregman said. “I wanted my swing to feel like it did right before I got hit. I felt good mechanically today.”</p><p>Bregman, the $175 million free-agent signee who figures to be a key factor in how far this team can go in the postseason, continues to marvel his fellow Cubs with what he’s doing, by merely taking the field so quickly after what happened.</p><p>“I’m not surprised that he’s performing when he’s back on the field. I’m surprised that he’s back on the field,” manager Craig Counsell said. “Him being back on the field is what we should all appreciate and admire.</p><p>“This is not normal that a player is back on the field right now after what he’s been through. You still see what he looks like, frankly, and that tells you what he’s still going through. That’s what I’m surprised by.</p><p>“But his performance, I don’t think it surprises you.”</p><p>Indeed, this is the sort of thing the Cubs long expected from the uber-accomplished Bregman, even back when he was mired in such a deep slump that he was getting booed at Wrigley Field.</p><p>His manager and teammates assumed he would finish the season with the sort of numbers he’s put up throughout his career, and wouldn’t you know it, that’s what happened.</p><p>Thanks to a huge second half, Bregman wrapped the campaign with 28 home runs — the third-highest total of his career — and a right-where-it’s-supposed-to-be .819 OPS.</p><p>“The first four months of the season, I don’t know what that was. I’m embarrassed to have put that on tape,” Bregman said. “But the last two months of the season, that’s who I am as a player. I’m proud to know that, no matter how big of a hole I dug myself, I found my way back out of it and [finished with an OPS] over .800.</p><p>“I learned a lot this year, and I feel like I got better as a pro.”</p><p>After the Cubs scored just nine runs over their five previous games, they wrapped their regular season with a half dozen on Sunday, finally escaping the chilly, windy conditions of Wrigley Field and Fenway Park in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/25/cubs-red-sox-game-moved-boston-weather-fenway-park-tampa-bay-florida-tropicana-field" >a game relocated to Florida</a>.</p><p>While it might not wipe away all fan concerns over what’s possible in the postseason, it was a good day for the bats — they banged out 13 hits — ahead of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/26/cubs-playoff-matchup-padres-nl-wild-card-standings-mlb-postseason-san-diego-phillies-diamondbacks" >a trip to San Diego</a> for a best-of-three playoff series against the Padres.</p><p>There are <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/26/cubs-regular-season-finale-playoffs-mlb-postseason-nl-wild-card-standings-offense-lineup-pitching-rotation" >a lot of questions following the Cubs</a> as they head to the West Coast and the lights get their brightest. But their long-held championship-level goals are still in front of them.</p><p>And the belief hasn’t left the clubhouse.</p><p>“When you show up to spring training, that’s what you work the whole offseason for, to start this and be able to play meaningful games in October. That’s exactly what we’ve done,” lefty reliever Ryan Rolison said. “It hasn’t been perfect this year. We’ve been through a lot of adversity, guys stepping up in spots. Now we’re here, and we’re going to make some noise here in October.”</p><p>“When we put games together,” righty reliever Ryan Zeferjahn said, “I don’t know who can beat us.”</p><p>For Bregman, the two-time World Series champ who’s done <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/14/cubs-alex-bregman-career-playoff-games-postseason-world-series-braves-nl-wild-card-standings-mlb-playoff-matchups-carson-kelly-sprint-speed" >more than almost any other hitter in postseason history</a>, he sees in these Cubs the right ingredients for the sort of success he’s had previously in his career.</p><p>“A togetherness. An attention to detail,” he said. “Guys that know what they do well and know what they need to do to prepare.</p><p>“When it comes to the playoffs, it comes down to executing. You’re playing against the best teams in the world. If you do that, you’re in a good spot.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports-media/2026/09/27/chicago-cubs-white-sox-mlb-postseason-playoffs-padres-astros-nbc-nbcsn-peacock-streaming-prime-video-xfinity-fubo-youtubetv" >Cubs, White Sox fans take one on chin from wild-card TV</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Cubs’ Kevin Gausman, with nagging shoulder, unsure if he’d be ready for possible Game 1 start vs. Padres
entries.summary: <p>ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Will <b>Kevin Gausman</b> be ready for Game 1 of the postseason?</p><p>“I don’t know,” the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>’ right-hander said Sunday. “That’s a tough [question to answer].”</p><p><b>Jed Hoyer</b>’s front office made Gausman — who <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/23/cubs-magic-number-playoffs-clinch-nl-wild-card-standings-kevin-gausman-shoulder-injury" >banged his left shoulder on a diving tag play</a> last week — the headlining piece of its trade-deadline haul, a suite of win-now moves that showed the belief in a Cubs team capable of winning a championship. In addition to a track record of success in 14 big league seasons, he starred during the Blue Jays’ run to the World Series last year.</p><p>But at the most critical time of the year — the time Gausman was acquired for — the Cubs are faced with the possibility he might not be available to start in their opening-round, best-of-three series against the Padres, which begins Tuesday in San Diego.</p><p>Gausman threw what he called a “normal-ish” bullpen session Sunday in Florida, describing it as “a step in the right direction.”</p><p>“I’m going to go out and give everything I’ve got,” Gausman said. “But if I feel like I can’t give this team a chance to win, or pitch the way I know I can, then I need to be smart and think about these guys and not myself.</p><p>“The goal is to get to the World Series, in any shape or form. I’m ready for whatever.”</p><p>It’s possible Gausman wouldn’t be the Cubs’ top choice to start Game 1, anyway.</p><p>They have several options, lefty <b>Matthew Boyd</b>, who will be on regular rest, among them. Lefty <b>Shota Imanaga</b> threw only 12 pitches in a planned short outing Sunday, keeping him available. By Game 2 on Wednesday, both righty <b>Clay Holmes</b> and lefty <b>David Peterson</b> will be on regular rest, as well.</p><p>And then there’s the fact that Gausman hasn’t been as effective as hoped, at times, swinging back and forth between excellent starts and bumpy ones. All told, he had a 4.83 ERA in his nine regular-season starts after coming to the Cubs.</p><p>But undoubtedly, of the Cubs’ options, Gausman is among the better ones and, given his experience, the kind of guy you’d want on the mound in a playoff start.</p><p>We’ll see if the Cubs will be able to send him out there.</p><h3><b>Bregman at third?</b></h3><h3></h3><p>After homering twice in Sunday’s win over the Red Sox, <b>Alex Bregman</b> is looking like himself at the plate again.</p><p>But after taking a foul ball off the face and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/23/cubs-alex-bregman-face-injury-return-matt-shaw-bunt-daniel-palencia-stats" >suffering multiple facial fractures</a> just a week ago, is he ready to get back in the field, where he’s played Gold Glove caliber third base this season?</p><p>“I’ll do whatever [manager <b>Craig Counsell</b>] wants me to do,” Bregman said. “I took ground balls [Saturday]. I’ll take ground balls again [Monday]. I’ll be available for whatever he needs. If he wants me to play wherever, I’m available.</p><p>“I want to play third, but I’ll do whatever it takes.”</p><h3><b>PCA goes 162</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Center fielder <b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b> got one at-bat before being removed Sunday, but it counted as his 162nd appearance of the season, another line on his MVP resume.</p><p>“That’s a special number,” Counsell said. “He’s done a number of special things this year, but that number is special to players.”</p><h3><b>Playoff game times</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The league announced start times for postseason games Sunday, and Cubs fans <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports-media/2026/09/27/chicago-cubs-white-sox-mlb-postseason-playoffs-padres-astros-nbc-nbcsn-peacock-streaming-prime-video-xfinity-fubo-youtubetv" >better be ready to stay up late</a>.</p><p>Games 1 and 2 of the team’s best-of-three series against the Padres are set for 9 p.m. Central on Tuesday and Wednesday. The start time for an if-necessary Game 3 depends on how many series are still going come Thursday.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports-media/2026/09/27/chicago-cubs-white-sox-mlb-postseason-playoffs-padres-astros-nbc-nbcsn-peacock-streaming-prime-video-xfinity-fubo-youtubetv" >Cubs, White Sox fans take one on chin from wild-card TV</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Illinois defensive coordinator Bobby Hauck out after 4 games
entries.summary: <p>CHAMPAIGN — Illinois defensive coordinator Bobby Hauck has parted ways with the program just four games into his first season, coach Bret Bielema announced Sunday.</p><p>Bielema had hired the former Montana head coach to replace Aaron Henry, who left to be co-defensive coordinator at Notre Dame.</p><p>The Illini (2-2, 0-1 Big Ten) <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/college-sports/2026/09/26/illinois-has-no-answers-for-ohio-state-receiver-jeremiah-smith" >lost 42-19 at Ohio State</a> on Saturday and enter this week 100th nationally in scoring defense, 111th in total defense and 119th in pass defense.</p><p>"Coach Hauck reached out to me early this morning and asked to meet ahead of our planned meeting time," Bielema said. "We met and mutually agreed that a change in leadership was in the best interests of our defense. Coach Hauck and I agreed this is the best path forward for our staff, and most importantly, our student-athletes, at this time. I would like to thank Bobby for his work with our program."</p><p>Bielema did not announce a successor to Hauck, who was hired less than a week after he announced his retirement from Montana in February.</p><p>"I enjoyed being a part of the staff here at Illinois and working alongside Coach Bielema every day," Hauck said. "I am very appreciative of the opportunity to be here and thankful for all of the hard work from the players, coaches, and staff. I wish Illinois the best of luck."</p><p>Illinois hosts Purdue on Saturday.<br></p>

entries.title: Veteran slugger Randal Grichuk found 'perfect marriage' in midseason deal with White Sox
entries.summary: <p><b>Randal Grichuk</b>’s renaissance campaign with the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> — capped with a go-ahead two-run home run in Sunday’s season-ending 4-2 win over the Rockies — began inauspiciously. Designated for assignment by the Yankees on April 29 after a slow start, he spent days considering offers before the Sox rushed in late.</p><p>“They called at the last minute — the day I was making my decision [May 4] was the day that <b>[Austin] Hays</b> got hurt,” Grichuk told the Sun-Times. “It wasn’t the best opportunity for a guaranteed role. We knew there was a chance that it was just for when Hays got healthy.”</p><p>The White Sox needed a right-handed bat to mash lefties, but the fit was narrow.</p><p>“My first day in Anaheim, I was like, ‘Why did I sign up? There's a million outfielders,’” Grichuk recalled.</p><p>Not only did the 35-year-old Grichuk pound lefties — his .654 slugging percentage against southpaws was tops in MLB (min. 170 PA) — but the well-traveled slugger became a crucial veteran presence. The youthful Sox clubhouse had a zillion self-referential t-shirts this season, but one featuring a photo of Grichuk set against block lettering of “WORLD’S GREATEST DAD” was a mainstay.</p><p>“[<b>Andrew Benintendi</b>’s] a great veteran, and he's definitely been awesome for the guys,” Grichuk said. “He's a little more reserved. So filling a void, so to speak, of being older, being a little bit more vocal, it's all fallen together in a perfect marriage.”</p><p>For someone with over 200 career homers, Grichuk has a very level swing. To get his hard contact in the air, he needs to catch the ball out in front. In order to do that, Grichuk needed a team that was comfortable with him being aggressive.</p><p>“He’s at 11 years of service time and has never walked, why at 35-years-old is he going to carry an above-average walk rate?” said Sox hitting coach <b>Derek Shomon</b>, expressing such comfort. “He is at his best when he’s getting off multiple swings inside the strike zone.”</p><p>With the Sox in 2026, Grichuk was at his best often.</p><h3><b>Doyle peaking at the right time?</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Outfielder <b>Brenton Doyle </b>still hasn’t walked since the White Sox acquired him at the August trade deadline. And during an early September stretch of right-handed opposing starters, he went almost two weeks without cracking the starting lineup.</p><p>But time on the sidelines allowed Doyle to practice the recommended tweaks to his setup made by Sox hitting coaches, aimed at moving his hands further from his body to enable a looser, more powerful swing.</p><p>“Once I started getting in [the lineup] more consistently, I’ve been able to trust the [work] I was putting in, in the [batting] cage, and results showed pretty instantly,” Doyle said.</p><p>After a two-run shot on Sunday, Doyle has homered three times in his last five games.</p><h3><b>Primed for playoff level information security</b></h3><h3></h3><p>When field coordinator <b>Chris Denorfia</b> was hired last December, he arrived with intent to monitor pitch-tipping, sign-stealing and other tells for a young roster not acquainted with a major-league level of scrutiny on these details.</p><p>“We are kind of teaching that on the fly to a lot of these guys,” Denorfia said. “We make sure that they have the correct information in a digestible atmosphere and a digestible form. And sometimes they work, sometimes they don't.”</p><p>The Sox are headed out to play the Astros after all. It can’t hurt to be prepared.</p>

entries.title: Cubs, White Sox fans take one on chin from wild-card TV
entries.summary: <p>Chicago baseball fans got the shaft when MLB released the schedule Sunday for the Cubs’ and White Sox’ wild-card series. NBC has the rights to the first-round matchups, but Games 1 and 2 for the Cubs and Sox were relegated to the network’s streaming service, Peacock, and NBC Sports Network, to which you might not have access.</p><p>The ballyhooed Red Sox-Yankees rivalry — which the nation always is subjected to more than necessary — naturally was given the prime-time spot on over-the-air NBC for the first two games of its series. The network also will air the first two games of the Phillies-Braves series in the afternoon. The best-of-three wild-card series are scheduled to run Tuesday to Thursday.</p><p>To watch Games 1 and 2 of Cubs-Padres and White Sox-Astros, fans must watch on Peacock, which costs $12.99 per month, or NBCSN, which is available on Comcast’s Xfinity system and streamers Fubo and YouTube TV. Though Xfinity and YouTube TV are two of the largest pay-TV providers in the country, NBCSN is missing from services such as DirecTV and Astound/RCN.</p><p>For the Sox, Games 1 and 2 are scheduled for 4 p.m. For the Cubs, they’re set for 9. The start time for a possible Game 3 of either series will depend on how many series are still going.</p><p>These aren’t the first major postseason games stuck on a streamer. The NFL put the Packers-Bears playoff game in January on Prime Video, but it was available locally over the air. The NBA streamed 28 first- and second-round playoff games exclusively on Peacock (seven, which also aired on NBCSN) and Prime Video (21) last season.</p><p>But they are the first MLB postseason games to air on a streaming service. It was part of NBC’s deal that gave it “Sunday Night Baseball,” which had aired on ESPN for 36 seasons, and the wild-card round. The rest of the American League playoffs will air on TBS; Fox and FS1 have the rest of the National League playoffs. The World Series will air on Fox.</p><p>Here’s some good news: NBC will continue its use of local analysts on national broadcasts. Steve Stone will be on the call for the Sox’ series, and Jim Deshaies will be in the booth for the Cubs’ series.</p>
